body.statement: For the TV-SACE and RM-SACE estimands of Comment et al., among all nonparametric full laws that reproduce \(P\) and satisfy the maintained restrictions, including the additional audited restriction \(D(0)\leq D(1)\), the set of resulting standardized surface pairs is exactly \(\Theta_I(P)\).  Necessity follows from the readmission-specific survivor-capacity inequalities, and every measurable family \(\nu_x\in\mathcal N_x\) admits a measurable full-law lift of \((D(0),R(0),D(1),R(1))\) that preserves \(\mu_{0x}\) and \(\mu_{1x}\), satisfies \(D(0)\leq D(1)\), and reproduces \(P\).  Thus \(\Theta_I(P)\) is sharp for the monotonicity-restricted nonparametric class.  No equality with \(\Theta_I(P)\) is asserted for a larger class that drops terminal monotonicity.
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it gives the exact nonparametric surface image under the separately audited terminal-monotonicity restriction, rather than extending that equality to an unrestricted nonmonotone class.
body.gap: Comment et al. define the estimands under a generally nonmonotone causal setup and fit a shared-frailty model; neither their model nor generic transport results prove the readmission-specific capacity equivalence and full-law lift for the monotonicity-restricted nonparametric class.
body.consumer: Clinicians obtain every TV-SACE/RM-SACE conclusion implied by the observed law and maintained terminal monotonicity; if that order is not credible, the three-horizon corollary still certifies nonidentification but the capacity equality is not claimed.
body.proof_tex:
The proof uses closed-relation coupling and coordinate gluing.  Define the latent compatibility class independently of the observed-law functional.  For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), let \(\mathcal Q_x\) be the set of probability laws on \(\mathcal E^4\) whose \((D(0),R(0))\)-margin is \(\mu_{0x}\), whose \((D(1),R(1))\)-margin is \(\mu_{1x}\), and which assign probability one to \(D(0)\leq D(1)\).  The within-arm margins obey the semicompeting-risk order by the maintained semicompeting-order assumption.  The causal identified surface set is the collection of target surfaces induced by measurable families \((Q_x:x\in\mathcal X)\) with \(Q_x\in\mathcal Q_x\) that, together with the observed treatment and censoring mechanisms, reproduce \(P\).  This class and its causal targets have been specified without using the definition of \(\Theta_I(P)\).

First, all primitives in the proposed image are observable-law functionals.  Positive covariate-cell support and treatment overlap give
\[
 \Pr_P(Z=z,X=x)>0
 \qquad(z\in\{0,1\},\ x\in\mathcal X),
\]
and full-horizon censoring support gives \(G_{zx}(L)\geq\gamma>0\).  Thus all conditioning and inverse weights in the established IPCW-recovery lemma are well defined.  By that lemma, consistency, conditional exchangeability, arm-specific independent censoring, and the two support assumptions identify \(\mu_{zx}\), including its atom at \(\infty\).  Marginalization and integration then identify \(d_x\), \(\zeta_x\), \(b_x\), \(K_x\), \(s_x\), and \(S\).

For necessity, fix \(Q_x\in\mathcal Q_x\), and let \(\nu_x\) be its \((D(0),R(1))\)-margin.  Its margins are \(d_x\) and \(\zeta_x\).  For every \(u\in[0,\tau]\) and Borel \(B\subseteq\mathcal E\), terminal monotonicity gives the event inclusion
\[
 \{D(0)>u,R(1)\in B\}
 \subseteq
 \{D(1)>u,R(1)\in B\}.
\]
Taking \(Q_x\)-probabilities and using the treated within-arm margin gives
\[
 \nu_x((u,\infty]\times B)
 \leq \mu_{1x}(D(1)>u,R(1)\in B)
 =K_x(u,B).
\]
This holds for every mark set \(B\), not merely for the unmarked survival margin, and hence \(\nu_x\in\mathcal N_x\) by the survivor-capacity definition.

For sufficiency, fix \(x\) and \(\nu_x\in\mathcal N_x\).  Regard \(\alpha=\nu_x\) and \(\beta=\mu_{1x}\) as probability measures on two copies of \(\mathcal E^2\); their second-coordinate margins both equal \(\zeta_x\).  Introduce the closed relation
\[
 \mathcal R
 =\{((d_0,v),(d_1,v')):v=v',\ d_0\leq d_1\}.
\]
It is closed because the diagonal and the order graph are closed in the compact metric carrier \(\mathcal E\).

We verify the compact-set inequalities in the established Strassen closed-relation lemma.  The capacity inequalities imply
\[
 \alpha([u,\infty]\times B)\leq\beta([u,\infty]\times B)
 \qquad(u\in\mathcal E,\ B\in\mathscr B(\mathcal E)).                 \tag{1}
\]
For \(0<u\leq\tau\), choose \(u_k\uparrow u\) with \(u_k<u\), apply the defining inequality to \((u_k,\infty]\times B\), and use continuity from above.  At \(u=0\), (1) is equality because the second margins coincide.  At \(u=\infty\), (1) is the boundary cut \((\tau,\infty]=\{\infty\}\), so the horizon atom is included.

Let \(A\subseteq\mathcal E^2\) be compact and put \(U=\mathcal R(A)\), viewing \(U\) as a subset of the second copy of \(\mathcal E^2\).  Compactness of \(A\), closedness of \(\mathcal R\), and compactness of the product imply that \(U\) is compact.  For each mark \(v\), its section is empty or a closed upper interval \([h(v),\infty]\).  For finite \(a\),
\[
 \{v:h(v)\leq a\}
 =\operatorname{proj}_v\!\left(A\cap([0,a]\times\mathcal E)\right),
\]
which is compact; hence \(h\) is Borel measurable on the nonempty sections.  On nested finite grids of \([0,\tau]\), round each finite \(h(v)\) down to \(\underline h_n(v)\), while retaining the \(\infty\) and empty sections.  The resulting \(U_n\) decrease to \(U\), and every \(U_n\) is a finite disjoint union of sets \([q,\infty]\times B_{nq}\), with Borel, pairwise disjoint mark sets \(B_{nq}\).  Summing (1) over these disjoint pieces and passing to the decreasing limit yields
\[
 \alpha(A)\leq\alpha(U)\leq\beta(U)=\beta(\mathcal R(A)).             \tag{2}
\]
The Strassen lemma applied to (2) supplies a coupling of \((D(0),R(1))\sim\nu_x\) and \((D(1),R'(1))\sim\mu_{1x}\) supported on \(R(1)=R'(1)\) and \(D(0)\leq D(1)\).  Identifying the equal mark coordinates gives a law \(\pi_x\) of \((D(0),D(1),R(1))\).

Reorder \(\mu_{0x}\) as the law of \((R(0),D(0))\).  This law and \(\pi_x\) have the same \(D(0)\)-margin \(d_x\).  The established compact-coordinate gluing lemma therefore gives a law \(Q_x\) of \((R(0),D(0),D(1),R(1))\) satisfying
\[
 \mathcal L_{Q_x}(D(0),R(0))=\mu_{0x},\qquad
 \mathcal L_{Q_x}(D(1),R(1))=\mu_{1x},\qquad
 Q_x\{D(0)\leq D(1)\}=1.                                            \tag{3}
\]
The within-arm strict event orders are inherited from the fixed margins.  No density or rank condition is used in this lift.

Because \(\mathcal X\) is finite, \(x\mapsto Q_x\) is automatically a measurable probability kernel.  Draw \(X\) with masses \(p_x\); conditionally on \(X=x\), draw the potential path from \(Q_x\), draw \(Z\) independently of that path with probability \(e(x)\), and draw \(C\) from its observed conditional law given \((Z,X)\), independently of the potential path.  Consistency forms the factual event path.  Equation (3) gives exactly \(\mu_{zx}\) in arm \(z\) and cell \(x\), while the construction preserves the observed laws of \((X,Z,C)\).  Arm-specific independent censoring makes the corresponding conditional observed-history factorization the same as under \(P\).  Since \(O\) is a measurable function of these variables, the lifted law reproduces \(P\).

It remains to relate the causal targets to the observed-law image.  Terminal monotonicity gives
\[
 \{D(0)>t,D(1)>t\}=\{D(0)>t\}.                                      \tag{4}
\]
For \((r,t)\in\mathcal H_\eta\), the target-domain definition gives \(S(t)\geq\eta>0\), so conditioning is legitimate.  Conditioning first on \(X\), and using (4), \(\nu_x\), and \(b_x\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\Pr\{R(1)\leq r\mid D(0)>t,D(1)>t\}
-\Pr\{R(0)\leq r\mid D(0)>t,D(1)>t\}\\
&\quad=\frac{\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x
 \{\nu_x((t,\infty]\times[0,r])-b_x(r,t)\}}{S(t)}
=\theta_\nu(r,t).                                                    \tag{5}
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(q\in\mathcal E\) and \(0\leq a\leq t\), including \(q=\infty\),
\[
 \min\{q,a\}=a-\int_0^a\mathbf 1\{q\leq r\}\,dr.
\]
Integrating this bounded identity under the two conditional laws, subtracting, and using (5) yields
\[
 E[\min\{R(1),a\}-\min\{R(0),a\}\mid D(0)>t,D(1)>t]
 =-\int_0^a\theta_\nu(r,t)\,dr
 =\rho_\nu(a,t).                                                     \tag{6}
\]

Necessity puts every compatible causal surface in \(\Theta_I(P)\); the measurable construction attains every member of that image while preserving all maintained restrictions and \(P\).  Equations (5)--(6) prove, rather than define, the equality with the causal target.  Thus the characterization is sharp for the nonparametric class with \(D(0)\leq D(1)\).  If terminal monotonicity is removed, both the necessity inclusion and (4) can fail, so no equality for that larger class follows.
